Section / page: Sec.2.1 Solution 4 (6.4) -- the digest floor at the extremes (p.4)
Item: As k->0 the floor vanishes (a mostly-safe swarm is cheap to digest); as k->N/2 the floor grows to Theta(N) bits for any fixed review budget m<<N, so past a load-bearing density 'summarize' degenerates to 'list' -- the formal justification for keeping the dangerous set small by construction.

Section / page: Sec.2.1 Solution 5 (6.5, starred) -- adversarial load-bearing estimation (p.4)
Item: Against an adaptive adversary the bound becomes log2 C(N,k') with k' the indistinguishability-class size; the adversary attacks by inflation (drive the floor toward Theta(N), a legibility denial-of-service) or mimicry (make critical artifacts appear inert); the defense is building the digest only from signals the agent cannot forge, with the residue an inspection game sharing Conjecture III.11.1's Becker condition.

Section / page: Sec.2.2 Solution 6 (7.1) -- no monotone transform unifies discovery and attention (p.4-5)
Item: Discovery maximizes capability fit (Eq I.2); the attention queue maximizes regret-if-ignored=stakes*irreversibility*anomaly (Eq I.3); high-fit/low-risk and low-fit/high-risk items order oppositely under the two, so no strictly monotone scalar transform can identify them.
